agree.reason: The reasons are clear and the partners admit their own part, but the 11 remote hires who live within two hours get sympathy and no support, so a resisting reader has little reason to stay rather than push back or leave.

honest.reason: No numbers are invented and the dates are read correctly, but 'how we came across as a team cost us the project' goes further than the clients' comment, which doesn't say it was what decided the outcome.

works_the_facts.reason: The figures are repeated as given and never worked: the 30% delay isn't turned into time, nobody points out that 11 of the 15 remote hires get no special arrangement, and there's no estimate of what keeps happening if nothing changes.

right_comparison.reason: The draft gives reasons but never describes what continuing fully remote would look like, such as more lost bids or slower development, and it leaves out that 5 of 6 project leads already come in three days, which would show how far the change has already gone.

qualification.reason: The partner offered a six-month review with staff, and the draft doesn't mention it, so the policy reads as permanent with no date or measure the reader can check.

objections.reason: The objection 'you hired me as remote' is acknowledged but not met: the $150 commuting support, the desks arriving in August and the six-month review are all left out, and the draft never says plainly that there are no other exceptions.

fit.reason: It is a one-page email in a sensible order, but it is signed with placeholders even though the writer knew Paul's name, and it leaves out the meeting time, the room and the HR contact.
